messages.author: 38a3aacdb5d6f07c
messages.subject: "random effects" interactions?
parts:
Dear INLA community,

Categorical variables g1 and g2 are not nested in my data. In lme4 I would write my desired model as:

y ~ 1 + (1 | g1) + (1 | g2) + (1 | g1:g2)

What is the equivalent in INLA? Suppose my model without the interaction random effects is:

y ~ 1 + f(g1, model="iid") + f(g2, model="iid")

Thanks so much!
Shira

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] "random effects" interactions?
parts:
INLA does not have any concept of 'nested random effects' hence you're
free to do what you want.

with

y ~ f(g1, model="iid") + f(g2, model="iid")

you're just specifying which components in 'f(g1...)' and 'f(g2...)'
that goes into the linear predictor for y'

if 'u' is the first term, 'v' the second, then with normal data,

y[1] ~ N( intercept + u[g1[1]] + v[g2[1]], ..)
y[2] ~ N( intercept + u[g1[2]] + v[g2[2]], ..)
y[3] ~ N( intercept + u[g1[3]] + v[g2[3]], ..)


etc.

> g1 = as.factor(c("a", "b", "a", "a"))
> g2 = as.factor(c(1,2,2,1))
> g1g2 = as.factor(paste(g1,g2,sep=""))
> cbind(g1,g2,g1g2)
g1 g2 g1g2
[1,] 1 1 1
[2,] 2 2 3
[3,] 1 2 2
[4,] 1 1 1
> g1g2
[1] a1 b2 a2 a1
Levels: a1 a2 b2


then its just

formula = y ~ 1 + f(g1) + f(g2) + f(g1g2)



there is a backdoor-option to define joint priors for the
hyperparameters, if you *really* need it..

H

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] "random effects" interactions?
parts:
On Fri, 2019-09-06 at 08:53 -0700, shira wrote:
> Thanks so much! So the interaction g1g2 has to be first created as
> another variable in the dataset? There is no syntax like in lme4
> ("g1:g2") to do it directly in the formula?

only if you have this as fixed effects, then

y ~ .... + g1 + g2 + g1:g2

or

y ~ ... + g1*g2

would be allowed.


there is no '(1|g1)' notation, simply because, we do not rely on this structure.

of'course, if someone wrote a translator, we would be happy to add it

H

--

there is no '(1|g1)' notation, simply because, we do not rely on this structure.

Right, I envisioned something more like:
 
y ~ 1 + f(g1, model="iid") + f(g2, model="iid") + f(g1:g2, model="iid") 

But will instead create a g1g2 variable and do:

y ~ 1 + f(g1, model="iid") + f(g2, model="iid") + f(g1g2, model="iid")
of'course,  if someone wrote a translator, we would be happy to add it

Something for me to aspire to!

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] "random effects" interactions?
parts:
On Fri, 2019-09-06 at 09:24 -0700, shira wrote:
> y ~ 1 + f(g1, model="iid") + f(g2, model="iid") + f(g1:g2,
> model="iid")

exactly, that would not work, as it interpret 'g1:g2' as a variable
on its own, it will not be expanded. the ``fixed effect'' part, is
passed through some 'lm()' internals, so it does what you expect them to do.

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] "random effects" interactions?
parts:
I have been thinking about implementing something like f(g1:g2, model=“iid”) or f(list(g1, g2), model=“interaction”) in the inlabru package, where we already do special interpretation of the model inputs. It’s some way down on the priority list, since the same effect can be obtained by prespecifying dummy variables in the input data.

Finn

yes, since in this case, 'g1:g2' is nothing else than a constructed
variable as you say, it does not add much.

it would be more useful to add some support for

(1 + x | g1)

and similar constructs from lme, but its mostly just a translator, as
the model="intslope" in INLA does the above, so its a question again,what the real gain is.

H
